Neither establishes the whole claim about practical reasoning, tool use and alignment. Continuing errors cannot prove that these problems will never go away, and improvements alone do not refute Marcus's forecast.
limitations: The formal and practical meanings of hallucination differ.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: The recurring core technical problems of LLMs are inherent to the technology and will not go away.

statement.excerpt: I think that the recurring core technical problems that we have seen (as discussed below) with LLMs aren’t going way; instead they inherent to the technology.
statement.document_title: Three years on, ChatGPT still isn't what it was cracked up to be – and it probably never will be

our_interpretation: The statement combines an indefinite forecast with an explanation based on the technology itself.
The post identifies unreliable reasoning, hallucinations, unreliable external-tool use, controllability and alignment among the recurring problems.
The ordinary reading concerns persistent practical failure patterns. It does not require mathematically perfect answers to every possible question.
Reducing error rates is relevant progress but does not by itself show that the recurring problems have gone away.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence establishes that the named practical failure patterns necessarily persist across the relevant LLM technology, rather than merely appearing in current implementations.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Independent, reproducible evidence shows that an in-scope LLM system has reliably overcome the named recurring problems across varied, unfamiliar tasks and realistic deployment conditions.

evidence.explanation: The paper supplies theoretical support under a definition involving computable models and ground-truth functions. That does not establish that all the practical failure patterns Marcus names are unavoidable at useful human-level reliability.

The authors identify training and evaluation incentives that reward guessing and propose changes. This challenges an unqualified claim of architectural inevitability, but does not demonstrate elimination of hallucinations or the other named problems.
The company reports both improvement and continuing hallucinations before the forecast. This establishes background persistence, not permanent necessity or a subsequent resolution.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Broad, independently replicated evidence that the named practical failures have been overcome within LLM technology, or a validated necessity result covering those failures under realistic conditions.
